title: Ukrainian forces withdraw from Avdiivka after four months of Russian assault
body:
The Battle of Avdiivka began on 10 October 2023 and ended on 17 February 2024, when Ukraine's commander-in-chief Oleksandr Syrskyi announced that Ukrainian forces were withdrawing from the town in Donetsk Oblast. He said the decision was taken to avoid encirclement and to preserve the lives and health of service personnel. The withdrawal was the first major decision of Syrskyi's tenure, after his appointment on 8 February 2024.

Ukrainian defenders included the 3rd Assault, 59th Motorized and 110th Mechanized Brigades. Russian forces included units of the 8th, 2nd Guards and 41st Combined Arms Armies, the 90th Guards Tank Division and Storm-Z penal units. Ukrainian commanders attributed the Russian breakthrough to artillery shortages caused by delays in European Union and United States military aid. They said Russian forces were firing about five shells for every Ukrainian one, and that Russia fielded more first-person-view drones.

Ukrainian authorities claimed Russian losses of 17,000 killed and 30,000 wounded, figures that cannot be independently verified. Russian losses were not officially confirmed. The civilian toll was recorded as 154 killed and six missing. Russian forces captured Avdiivka and several surrounding villages.
